title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
theological_headline: PKD reads Mercer's three levels — real, fake, real — as the structure of the fake fake that is finally true, his model for Christianity.
intro:
*Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?* appears once in the Exegesis, and PKD uses it for a single, precise purpose: the three-layer structure of Wilbur Mercer. Mercer surfaces as real, is exposed below that as a hoax, and beneath the hoax is real again — a nesting PKD takes as the very structure of a truth that survives being unmasked. (Lane B: PKD reading his own fiction as a logical model.)

The novel's better-known themes — empathy as the mark of the authentic, the tomb world, kipple — are not developed in the passage; the page keeps to the three-value logic PKD actually draws from it.
theological_synthesis:
The theological use is logical and Christological. In [18:1] PKD lays out *Do Androids Dream* as a three-level structure: Mercer real, then Mercer fake and fraud, then — bottom line — Mercer real. He says "this 3 level structure is the one *we* have vis-à-vis Christianity": a secret within a secret, A, Ā, A. The question "Is a fake fake real?" is answered "Yes" for Christianity in a two-value system, but PKD prefers a three-value one, where the reversal of the reversed does not restore the original A but yields A′ — "A reinterpreted," a deeper level that both is and is-not A.

Mercer's exposed-yet-real empathy figure thus becomes PKD's proof that a debunked sacred thing can be true at a level beneath its fraudulence. The novel supplies the formal engine — the fake fake that is real — for his claim that ordinary reality (A) is only a picture of the reinterpreted real (A′), and that Christianity's Mercer-like structure vindicates faith precisely by passing through the hoax rather than around it.

mentions.summary: Which is it: hallucination as reality (e.g., _3 Stigmata_ ) or reality as hallucination (e.g., Bishop Berkeley)? Stated this way, I think the latter. Reality (USA 1974) is hallucination, and can be voided through faith—whereupon the _absolute_ time and place ("Acts") appears. Thus _3 Stigmata_ and _Maze_ are total opposites: in _Maze_ reality is a hallucination. There is a real world behind it. But in _3 Stigmata_ hallucination becomes real—not: real becomes hallucination and hence departs. _Do Androids Dream_ ... reveals: - (1) Surface level: Mercer real (2) Below that: Mercer fake—hoax—fraud (3) Below that: Mercer real (Bottom Line) I think this 3 level structure is the one _we_ have vis-à-vis Christianity. A secret within a secret A, Ā, A. "Precious Artifact" (3 layer) was close. You have this: Q: "Is a fake fake real?" re Christianity: A: "Yes." — This is in terms of a 2-value system ("A or Ā"). If a _3_ -value system is used: — A becomes Ā by reversal. Then Ā is reversed, _not_ restoring A, but something else. A what? How does it differ from A, if at all? Answer: call it A ′. I say A′ "out A's A," in an ontological sense. It is a profoundly deeper, richer newer level than A, but also (paradoxically) it _is_ A. But A′ is not A. So: A′ _is_ and is-not A. — But: A′ is not Ā. The reversal of the reversed does not restore the original thing. I say, A is just a _picture_ of A′. Whatever that means. But it's so. Of the 3, only A′ is really real. A and A′ are identical, but A and Ā are false; only A′ is real. [...] Voice: "A′ is A _reinterpreted._ "
mentions.gloss: PKD reads Mercer's three levels — real, then fake and fraud, then real again — as the structure "*we* have vis-à-vis Christianity": A, Ā, A, a secret within a secret. The fake fake that is nonetheless real supplies his formal model for a sacred thing surviving its own unmasking. He extends it to a three-value logic where the doubly reversed yields not A but A′, "A reinterpreted" — the deeper real of which ordinary reality is only a picture. Empathy, the tomb world, and kipple are not treated; the novel is used for its fake-fake-real logic.
